claim: TS= searches Title, Abstract, Author Keywords and Keywords Plus
source_title: Web of Science Core Collection Advanced Search Field Tags

claim: Keywords Plus are words and phrases harvested from the titles of cited articles
source_title: Web of Science Core Collection quick reference guide (Clarivate; copy hosted by ULAKBIM)

claim: NEAR/x finds terms within x words of each other; NEAR without /x means 15 words; AND cannot be used inside a NEAR expression
source_title: Search Operators

claim: Left-hand truncation is allowed in Topic and Title searches, with at least three characters after the wildcard
source_title: Search Rules

claim: Quotation marks search for an exact phrase in Topic searches
source_title: Searching the Topic Field

claim: TITLE-ABS-KEY searches title, abstract and keywords; KEY combines author keywords, index terms, trade names and chemical names
source_title: Scopus Search Tips (Elsevier Developer Portal)

claim: Double quotation marks give a loose phrase: punctuation is ignored, hyphenated forms are treated as the loose phrase, wildcards work, and plurals and spelling variants are included; braces give an exact phrase
source_title: How can I best use the Advanced search? (Scopus Support Center)

claim: The asterisk replaces zero or more characters anywhere in a word, e.g. *tocopherol; a wildcard separated from a word by a hyphen or dot is dropped
source_title: Scopus Search Tips (Elsevier Developer Portal)

claim: W/n finds terms within n words in any order; PRE/n requires the first term to precede the second; operators are processed in the order OR, W/n and PRE/n, AND, AND NOT
source_title: How can I best use the Advanced search? (Scopus Support Center)

claim: Scopus applies lemmatisation to English words and most scientific terms unless an exact phrase is used, so wildcards are not needed for singular and plural forms
source_title: Search Tips: What makes a Scopus search complex? (Scopus Support Center)

claim: The Entry Date (ED) field holds NLM's Date Completed, when record processing ends
source_title: Ovid MEDLINE database guide

claim: As of April 2022, all journals indexed for MEDLINE are indexed automatically, with human review and curation of selected sets (for example clinical trials, genes and proteins) and random samples
source_title: Frequently Asked Questions about Indexing for MEDLINE

claim: MTIX, a neural network released in 2024, assigns MeSH from the title, abstract, publication year, indexing year and journal name; it was trained on MEDLINE citations published 2007 to 2022; automated indexing does not use full text
source_title: Frequently Asked Questions about Indexing for MEDLINE; NLM Technical Bulletin 457 (MTIX)

claim: Automated indexing is generally completed within 1 day of receipt; the average time for fully human indexing in FY 2021 was 145 days, excluding bibliographic data review
source_title: Frequently Asked Questions about Indexing for MEDLINE

claim: NLM typically does not re-index existing citations with new MeSH headings, so a new heading retrieves only citations indexed after its introduction; exceptions have been made for some publication types (Systematic Review in 2019; Network Meta-Analysis and Scoping Review for 2025)
source_title: Annual MeSH Processing for 2025 (NLM Technical Bulletin 461)

claim: From December 2026, citations in scope for MEDLINE that have no abstract in PubMed are given the IndexingMethod value NotIndexed and receive no MeSH terms unless an abstract is later supplied
source_title: PubMed Update: Data Updates Scheduled for 2027 Baseline (NLM Technical Bulletin 472)

claim: Descriptor D061218 was introduced in 2012; previous indexing: Depressive Disorder (1981-2011); entry terms include Refractory Depression and Treatment Resistant Depression
source_title: MeSH Browser record D061218

claim: The 'qualitative (maximizes sensitivity)' limit runs interview:.tw. or px.fs. or exp health services administration/, reported as 95% sensitivity and 70% specificity, from McMaster's Hedges project
source_title: Clinical Queries - Qualitative - Maximized Sensitivity - Ovid MEDLINE (OvidGO)

claim: Fully indexed Embase records (other than licensed MEDLINE records) are indexed manually from full text against Emtree; licensed MEDLINE records have MeSH mapped to Emtree; articles in press, in-process records, preprints and conference abstracts are indexed automatically from title, abstract and author keywords
source_title: How is Embase indexed? (Embase Support Center)

claim: Since February 2023, PubMed searches indexingmethod_automated and indexingmethod_curated retrieve automatically indexed and curated citations; fully human-indexed citations are medline[sb] NOT (indexingmethod_curated OR indexingmethod_automated)
source_title: Frequently Asked Questions about Indexing for MEDLINE

claim: ADJn finds terms in any order with up to n-1 words between (ADJ1 adjacent, ADJ3 up to 2 words between; n from 1 to 99); stop words count towards the distance; plain ADJ or a space means adjacent in order
source_title: Medline database guide; Stopwords and phrase searching in Ovid databases

claim: Ovid recommends one-to-one ADJn operations, because stroke adj4 (blood pressure or high blood pressure) could miss some combinations
source_title: Medline database guide

claim: * or $ truncate without limit; $n limits the characters added; # stands for exactly one character; ? for one or no character
source_title: Medline database guide

claim: Ovid ignores hyphens; when indexing title and abstract, - / ; + [ ] ( ) are converted to a space; run-time stop-word processing ignores and, as, for, from, is, of, that, the, this, to, was, were in searches (on by default)
source_title: Searching terms with hyphens; Stopwords and phrase searching in Ovid databases

claim: "search terms"[field:~N] in Title, Title/Abstract or Affiliation; N is the maximum number of words between the terms, 0 meaning adjacent; any order; a wildcard in the quoted terms makes PubMed ignore the proximity operator
source_title: PubMed User Guide

claim: * needs at least 4 characters before the first wildcard and turns off automatic term mapping; quoted phrases must be in the phrase index or the quotes are ignored; a hyphenated phrase not in the phrase index returns no results for that phrase
source_title: PubMed User Guide

claim: Nn finds terms a maximum of n words apart in any order (tax N5 reform matches tax that has been submitted for reform); Wn keeps the order; n up to 255; stop words count towards the distance; the Proximity search mode defaults to N5
source_title: How do I create a proximity search?; How are phrases searched?

claim: A hyphen acts as a proximity operator with distance zero, in the order entered; stop words are always ignored, even inside quotation marks
source_title: How are phrases searched?

claim: Since December 2025, an asterisk after fewer than three characters is removed (ph* becomes ph)
source_title: EBSCO research platforms roadmap

claim: NEAR/n finds terms within n words in either direction, NEXT/n in order; NEAR/1 means adjacent with no words between
source_title: Can I use Boolean operators, wildcards and proximity operators in Embase?

claim: * truncates, ? replaces one character, $ zero or one; wildcards work inside phrases; leading wildcards are not allowed; parentheses are executed first, then left to right, with no Boolean operator taking precedence
source_title: Can I use Boolean operators, wildcards and proximity operators in Embase?

claim: A hyphen in a search is treated as a hyphen or a space
source_title: How do I search for non-alphanumeric characters?

claim: NEAR/x: x is the maximum number of words that separate the terms; NEAR/0 means adjacent; operators are processed in the order NEAR/x, SAME, NOT, AND, OR
source_title: Search Operators

claim: TS=hydro-power finds hydro-power and hydro power; lemmatisation and stemming apply automatically to English terms, and are turned off by quotation marks, wildcards or Exact Search
source_title: Search Rules

claim: W/n gives the distance between words without order and PRE/n with order; to find adjacent terms use 0 (heart PRE/0 attack returns the same as "heart attack")
source_title: How do I search in Scopus?

claim: Elsevier announced a change from late 2025, to be completed in early 2026, to AND NOT, then AND, then OR; the Support Center page updated 2026-08-24 still lists OR, W/n and PRE/n, AND, AND NOT
source_title: Boolean searches in Scopus: understanding operator precedence and best practices (Scopus blog)

claim: Best Match is the default sort; citations are weighted by how many search terms are found and in which fields, with a boost for recent articles, and the top articles are re-ranked by a machine-learning model combining over 150 signals, built on relevance data from aggregated PubMed search logs
source_title: PubMed User Guide

claim: PubMed can display up to 10,000 results; Save and Citation Manager export all results up to 10,000; Collections and email up to 1,000; for larger sets the guide suggests reversing the sort order, dividing the set by date, narrowing the search, or FTP for bulk downloads
source_title: PubMed User Guide

claim: Google Scholar can only show up to 1,000 results for any search query and cannot provide bulk access; records are exported one at a time through Cite
source_title: Google Scholar search help

claim: Google Scholar aims to rank documents by weighing the full text, where a document was published, who wrote it, and how often and how recently it has been cited
source_title: About Google Scholar

claim: Relevance uses term frequency, TF/IDF, field of the hit, position, proximity and completeness; terms with a wildcard cannot contribute to the ranking; citedness, popularity and date are not included; default sort is date, newest first
source_title: What does relevance mean in Scopus?

claim: Sorting applies to the whole result set, not just the 2,000 displayed; up to 20,000 documents can be exported to file formats (2,000 to Mendeley)
source_title: How do I work with document search results?; How do I export documents from Scopus?

claim: Relevance considers how many search terms are found in title, abstract, keywords and Keywords Plus, with title and keywords weighted slightly more; summary records export up to 1,000 at a time depending on format, or 5,000 with limited fields (Fast 5000)
source_title: Search Results; Saving and Exporting Marked Lists

claim: Relevance score = log(term frequency) x inverse document frequency, summed over terms; OR searches are ranked by how many optional terms a record contains; registered users export up to 10,000 records at a time, anonymous users 500
source_title: How is the relevance ranking of articles calculated?; How do I export my search results?

claim: Only Basic Search results are relevancy ranked; the default limit for selecting, printing, emailing or exporting is 200 results, which institutions may change
source_title: Basic search; Selecting results (Ovid help)

claim: Relevance uses term frequency, field weighting, exact field matching and content attribute boosting; subject headings weigh most, then title, author keywords, abstract, authors and full text; newly published and peer-reviewed records are prioritised
source_title: How is relevance ranking determined in EBSCOhost?

claim: Elicit initially searches for up to 1,000 papers; per review, Pro users can add up to 5,000 papers, Scale 20,000 and Enterprise 40,000
source_title: Systematic Reviews in Elicit

claim: Hybrid semantic and BM25 search over the whole database, refinement using recency, citation count and journal signals, then a larger model re-ranks only the top 20 papers
source_title: How Consensus works

claim: The default model is ELAS u4: TF-IDF features with bigrams, a support vector machine classifier, the Maximum query strategy and a Balanced balancer; each labelling decision starts training a new model if none is training
source_title: ASReview LAB documentation: AI models; Screening

claim: An optional threshold of not-relevant records since the last relevant record prompts the user to stop or continue; no threshold is set by default; the documentation says the ideal threshold is still actively researched and that when to stop is left to the user; no estimate of remaining relevant records is given
source_title: ASReview LAB documentation: Progress and results; Screening

claim: Unscreened records are scored by a support vector machine on TF-IDF features of one- to three-word phrases and shown in score order; since V6.17.0.0 the model retrains every 25 items while fewer than 250 have been screened, decreasing to every 400 items after 15,000
source_title: Machine learning functionality in EPPI-Reviewer (v10); Latest changes V6.17.0.0 (30/09/2025)

claim: No stopping aid in the live screening workflow; guidance says there are no hard and fast rules and offers a resource limit, a plateau of no new includes, or a baseline inclusion rate; the BUSCAR stopping rule is implemented only for priority-screening simulations (V6.18.0.0, 16/04/2026); the machine-learning guide recommends screening all items manually
source_title: Stopping criteria for priority screening (EPPI Centre manual); Latest changes V6.18.0.0

claim: The default title-and-abstract sort uses an active-learning model developed by EPPI-Centre; it starts after at least 25 votes with at least 2 included and 2 excluded
source_title: AI feature: Most relevant sorting

claim: Covidence does not recommend any criteria or rules for stopping screening before all studies have been voted on and does not remove studies on the basis of predicted relevance
source_title: Machine learning: the game changer for trustworthy evidence (blog); AI feature: Most relevant sorting

claim: Re-Rank reprioritises references as reviewers include and exclude them; a predictive reporting tool gives a conservative prediction of the number of relevant records not yet identified; the current public product page does not describe the report and the user guide requires a login
source_title: The case for artificial intelligence in systematic reviews (white paper); DistillerAI product page

claim: A support vector machine trained on unigrams, bigrams and MeSH terms rates records after at least 50 decisions with at least 5 includes and 5 excludes, when the user clicks Compute Ratings; the help pages give no stopping guidance
source_title: How to use ratings and relevance ranking in Rayyan

claim: The Create Date (DT) field holds the date a record was added to PubMed; Ovid recommends DT for searches across parts of years and suggests saving the unique identifiers of each run and using NOT to find the difference; the Update Date (UP) resets with each annual reload
source_title: Limiting searches to time spans (OvidGO); Medline database guide

claim: [crdt] is when the citation was first created in PubMed and is recommended for checking citations added since a query was last run; [edat] is set to the publication date when a citation is added more than twelve months after publication; [dcom] is used by NLM for internal processing; none of these is searched by All Fields
source_title: PubMed User Guide

claim: MEDLINE citations were updated with 2026 MeSH; while the automated indexing algorithm was retrained it assigned some 2025 MeSH terms to new citations, which are to be updated to 2026 MeSH when retraining is complete
source_title: PubMed 2026 baseline released (NLM Technical Bulletin)

claim: Best Match re-ranks the top results with a machine-learning algorithm combining over 150 signals and is not designed for comprehensive or systematic searches
source_title: How does the PubMed Best Match feature work? (KA-03719)

claim: The /sd field (entry date, 'since date') defines when records were added to Embase; the entry date can mark both a record's first appearance (article in press or in process) and its full indexing
source_title: How do I use the calendar tool?; Embase release notes (July 2023)

claim: ORIG-LOAD-DATE is when a record was first loaded into Scopus; records may be re-loaded, and LOAD-DATE is the latest load; documented in developer documentation, not in the end-user search help checked
source_title: Elsevier Developer Portal: IR, CRIS and VIVO

claim: The advanced-search field-tag page lists publication-date fields (PY, which includes Early Access year; FPY; DOP) but no field for the date a record was added to the Core Collection
source_title: Web of Science Core Collection Advanced Search Field Tags

claim: EM searches the Entry Date, the date a record was added to CINAHL, in YYYYMM or YYYYMMDD format; a hyphen before or after the date finds on-or-before or on-or-after
source_title: CINAHL database help

claim: Elicit's help says it is constantly updated, that the language-model APIs it uses have inherent randomness, and that users can't count on the same answer when asking a question more than once; its changelog is dated but carries no version numbers
source_title: Why does Elicit provide a different answer when I ask the same question again?; Changelog

claim: Consensus keeps a dated changelog without version numbers, updates its database weekly, and added a Paper Search mode described as deterministic on 14 May 2026; the help centre does not say whether natural-language searches return the same results over time
source_title: Consensus product changelog; Consensus research database
